Maya Torres: Heads-up — we're kicking off a short enablement for Vertex Health (renewal flagged, medium risk). want to align on a lightweight customer-facing guidance doc focused on caching, batching, and streaming patterns they can adopt without infra changes.
Omar Patel: +1. What are the most impact/lowest-effort items?
Maya Torres: my quick list: 1) session-level response caching (stitching user context into cache keys), 2) delta batching for multi-turn requests, 3) graceful stream fallback when long polls exceed SLOs. keep it customer-facing and prescriptive.
Jules Chen: For stitching: recommend "session_id:user_profile_hash:prompt_template" as key pattern. note: avoid storing PII, use hashed stable id.
Nadia R.: agree. also suggest LRU cache with a 48-72h TTL for conversational contexts for their typical cadence. reduces cold-token hits.
Maya Torres: ops suggestion: include a sample snippet they can paste into Node/Go SDKs. something like:
```js
// pseudo: session stitch cache key
const key = `${sessionId}:${sha1(userFingerprint)}:${promptId}`
if (cache.has(key)) return cache.get(key)
// otherwise call Redwood API and cache response
```
Omar Patel: For batching: propose "delta batching"—group only the new turns or appended tokens instead of re-sending full history. decreases token costs and keeps latency tight.
Jules Chen: add a note: for safety-sensitive customers, provide explicit instructions to stop batching for any requests tagged "PII=TRUE". make it an opt-in config flag in their integration.
Nadia R.: streaming fallback — recommend a 2-tier approach: 1) try streaming (SSE/websocket) with 1.5s per-chunk SLO, 2) if total generation predicted > 8s, switch to non-streaming async job + progress webhook. helps UX on flaky networks.
Maya Torres: this is great. Let's keep the doc 1 page: scope, 5 config snippets (cache key, TTL, delta-batch pseudocode, batch window, stream fallback), and a short checklist for CS handoff.
Jules Chen: I'll draft the code snippets and a short troubleshooting table: common symptoms -> quick remediations (e.g., repeated tokens -> increase cache key granularity).
Omar Patel: Can we add a tiny telemetry snippet customers can paste to surface incidents? something like: event("cache.miss", {reason, session_len, model, tokens})
Maya Torres: yes — add "health pulse" metrics to measure pre/post: avg latency, token spend per session, cache hit rate, aborted streams.
onboard-bot: Note: customer "Vertex Health" profile exists in workspace "vh-account-32". renewal_tag: "at-risk".
Nadia R.: Final ask from my side — include a one-paragraph coach script for CSMs to use during the enablement call. quick lines: what it solves, how to measure success, and rollback steps.
Maya Torres: timeline: Jules drafts by EOD tomorrow, Omar reviews, I'll run a 20m enablement call with the customer Wed.
Omar Patel: I'll add the telemetry snippet to their kibana dashboard template.
Jules Chen: drafting now — will ping here when ready. :memo:
Maya Torres: thanks team. tagging renewal owner @Nadia R. for context. :thumbsup:
